correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the one-dimensional Hilbert metric to an ordinary interval metric via an explicit increasing cross-ratio coordinate. Convexified separation then increases the coordinate span by at least the separation at every step, giving the exact floor formula with a monotone extremizing sequence. A direct algebraic cancellation proves equality of primal and reversed-polar Hilbert diameters. Arya–Mount Lemma 4.3 then yields the fully convexified diagonal inequality because ordinary and convexified packing coincide in one dimension. Boundaries, quantifiers, polarity ordering, and the large-separation sharpness of \(C=1\) were checked explicitly. The finite verifier is only a sanity check.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact base case of a concrete open problem from a recent geometry paper. It identifies precisely why the synchronization obstruction disappears in one dimension, gives the exact packing number rather than only an existence bound, and shows exact same-scale primal-polar duality for arbitrary nested intervals containing the origin. The result is not an arbitrary parameter slice: dimension one is the canonical model case for a dimension-free conjectural bound, and the exact formula can serve as a benchmark for higher-dimensional arguments and computations.
